entities.name: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad Fāsī
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Taqi al-Din Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Fāsī (died 1429), an eminent Arab Muslim scholar of the Mamluk Sultanate era, served as a distinguished Maliki qadi (judge) in Mecca and left an indelible mark on Islamic historiography through his meticulous chronicles of the holy city. His life, spanning the late 14th and early 15th centuries, was dedicated to scholarship in Hadith, fiqh (jurisprudence), and history, positioning him as a pivotal figure in preserving the religious and social fabric of Mecca during a period of significant political and economic flux under Cairo's distant rule. His works provide an invaluable window into the administration, intellectual life, and pilgrimage patterns of the Hijaz.

Al-Fāsī's most significant achievement lies in his monumental historical compilations, particularly *Shifāʾ al-gharām bi-akhbār al-Balad al-Ḥarām* (The Cure for Love through the History of the Holy City) and *al-ʿIqd al-thamīn fī tārīkh al-Balad al-Amīn* (The Precious Necklace on the History of the Secure City). These encyclopedic works systematically documented the topography, institutions, notable residents, and intellectual currents of Mecca across centuries, drawing upon a vast array of earlier sources, oral traditions, and his personal observations as a long-serving qadi. His methodology combined rigorous Hadith criticism with a genealogist's precision, creating a rich tapestry of Meccan life, including detailed accounts of the Kaaba, the Grand Mosque, and the various pilgrimage rites.

entities.summary:
Taqi al-Din Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Fasi (1373–1429 CE) was a preeminent Arab Muslim scholar, jurist, and historian whose monumental works significantly documented the religious and social fabric of Mecca during the Mamluk period. Born into a distinguished scholarly family in Mecca, al-Fasi dedicated his life to the pursuit of knowledge, excelling particularly in Hadith studies, Maliki jurisprudence, and historiography. His scholarly rigor and meticulous approach cemented his reputation as a leading intellectual figure of his era, bridging the intellectual traditions of the Hijaz with those of Mamluk Egypt and Syria.

Al-Fasi's most enduring contribution is his voluminous biographical dictionary, "al-ʿIqd al-thamīn fī tārīkh al-balad al-amīn" (The Precious Necklace on the History of the Secure City), a comprehensive record of over 2,000 personalities who lived in or visited Mecca. This work, along with his "Shifāʾ al-gharām bi-akhbār al-balad al-ḥarām" (The Healing of Passion in the News of the Sacred Land), provides an unparalleled source of information on Meccan topography, institutions, and its illustrious inhabitants, including scholars, rulers, and Sufis, from early Islam up to his own time. His meticulous compilation of biographies and historical accounts offers critical insights into the social, political, and intellectual dynamics of the holy city during a pivotal period of Islamic history.
